title: Can AI help edit a batch of course lessons from one recording day?
summary: Turn a batch of recorded lessons into separate teaching sequences with consistent practical conventions and enough flexibility for each lesson's explanation.
body_markdown:
## What you’ll take away


- Separate lessons by learning outcome, not just recording file.
- Reuse setup and delivery preferences across the batch.
- Keep examples and prerequisite explanations together within each lesson.


## Separate lessons by what they teach


A single long recording may contain several lessons, restarts, informal comments, and pickup lines. Identify the beginning and end of each instructional unit. Give it a meaningful name such as setting exposure manually rather than lesson three final.


For example, a photography course might record exposure, focusing, and composition in one session. Each needs a clear outcome and its own examples. A remark in the exposure section may belong in the focus lesson, but do not move it merely because the terminology overlaps. Decide whether it advances that lesson's actual explanation.


## Prepare the recordings with consistent boundaries


Start Wideframe with the recording set and a lesson outline. The[transcript-export recipe](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/export-transcript/) provides timecoded source text, while[splitting at pauses](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/split-by-silence/) can help separate long recordings into workable material. Paste a linked setup prompt into chat to add the task you need.


Keep lesson boundaries distinct from silence boundaries. A pause may occur inside an example, while a lesson transition may have little silence. Use the outline and the actual content to identify the units. Retain pickups with the lesson and script section they correct.


## Set practical conventions on one representative lesson


Choose one lesson that contains the usual elements: instructor explanation, a demonstration, a title, and a result. Decide how those elements should appear. This is where you establish understandable section naming, the role of the instructor's face, and when the viewer needs an uninterrupted screen or object view.


Apply the practical conventions to the remaining lessons, but do not copy the exact pacing. A complex worked example may need more time than a simple definition. Consistency means the learner recognizes how the course works, not that every video reaches its conclusion at the same second.


## Preserve the learning chain in each assembly


For each lesson, keep the prerequisite idea, demonstration, and result together. An instructor may explain a necessary concept in a later take more clearly than in the main recording. Use it where it helps, but make the final progression understandable to someone learning for the first time.


Remove production discussion and redundant restarts without removing useful restatement. A second explanation in simpler words can be valuable. If a lesson contains two independent outcomes, split it deliberately rather than letting the recording-day boundary decide the course structure.


## Keep the batch's deliverables distinguishable


Create one clearly named editable sequence per lesson. Maintain the relationship between the lesson title, sequence, caption file, and review export. A consistent naming convention is useful because a batch creates many similar files; it is not a substitute for checking that each contains the intended lesson.


Finish captions against the final spoken edits. Supply a course glossary for names and technical terms, then review each lesson's specific examples. A shared spelling preference can be reused, but a number in one lesson should not be copied into another merely because the surrounding wording is similar.


If the batch is already in Premiere, add and save the[organize-my-project recipe](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/organize-my-project/) in a blank Wideframe chat. Supply the lesson-to-source mapping and ask for one named bin and working sequence per lesson on a project copy. Its default grouping is not a curriculum plan, so provide the lesson boundaries explicitly. The organization pass prepares containers; it does not decide each lesson's teaching edit.


## Reuse the routine for the next module


Save the bounded preparation tasks that proved useful: source transcript output, lesson naming, or caption settings. Wideframe's[custom-skill recipe](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/build-a-skill/) supports defining a repeatable task. Confirm the new module's recordings and outputs each time rather than treating the old source paths as permanent.


The next recording day can arrive in the same structure while containing completely different teaching. Our[course-video overview](https://try.wideframe.com/blog/ai-video-editing-for-education-online-courses/) addresses the wider category. This workflow is for turning a recording batch into a coherent set of real lessons, not simply multiplying video files.
